title: Agile in Plain English: Values, Feedback and Adaptation
summary: Understand Agile as a mindset for delivering value under uncertainty rather than a synonym for Scrum.
plain_language_explanation: Agile favors close collaboration, frequent delivery, fast feedback and adaptation while still valuing planning, documentation and governance where they help outcomes.

title: Agile Values, Principles and Delivery Continuum
summary: Apply values and principles while selecting predictive, iterative, incremental, flow-based or hybrid approaches based on context.
body_outline: Start from customer value and uncertainty, not framework preference.
Use short feedback loops and incremental delivery to reduce risk.
Select iterative, flow-based or hybrid practices to fit context.
Keep governance proportional to risk and compliance needs.
Use working outcomes and feedback as evidence of progress.
Treat adaptation as disciplined learning, not uncontrolled change.

title: Flow, Small Batches, WIP and Value Delivery
summary: Use work visualization, small batches, WIP limits and flow metrics to reduce delay and improve predictability.
body_outline: Visualize work and workflow before optimizing individual utilization.
Reduce batch size and excessive work in progress.
Use lead time, delivery rate and WIP to understand system behavior.
Find queues, handoffs, rework and blocked work that delay value.
Balance flow with quality and sustainable pace.
Use trends for learning rather than weaponizing metrics against teams.

title: Product Thinking, Modern Agile Metrics and Enterprise Agility
summary: Connect team-level adaptability to product outcomes, psychological safety, distributed work, AI-enabled delivery and enterprise learning.
architecture_notes: Modern agile practice extends beyond ceremonies to product thinking, outcomes, flow, psychological safety, distributed teams, scaling, sustainability and AI-enabled work. Metrics should explain value and improvement, not merely count output.

title: Read-Only Agile Delivery Evidence Pack
summary: Review flow, feedback and outcome evidence without changing team commitments or governance.
steps: Confirm product or service outcome and current delivery approach.
Review work-in-progress, lead-time or cycle-time evidence if available.
Review recent customer/stakeholder feedback and outcome measures.
Identify blocked work, queues, handoffs, rework and recurring delays.
Review improvement experiments and whether they changed outcomes.
Document evidence-backed options without changing commitments, priorities or policies.

title: Agile Delivery Anti-Pattern Decision Tree
summary: Diagnose ceremony theatre, overloaded WIP, weak feedback, metric gaming and pseudo-agility before prescribing process changes.
diagnostic_order: Confirm the customer or business outcome before diagnosing process symptoms.
Check work-in-progress, queueing, handoffs and blocked-work evidence.
Assess whether feedback arrives early enough to change decisions.
Separate output-volume problems from quality or value problems.
Check whether metrics are driving gaming or unhealthy comparison.
Change ways of working only through team and governance authority appropriate to the context.

title: Agile Foundations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment across values, life-cycle selection, flow, feedback and modern agile measurement.

assessment_items.question: Does Agile mean no planning?
assessment_items.answer: No. Agile favors adaptive planning and frequent feedback; the amount and horizon of planning should fit context.

assessment_items.question: Why can high individual utilization reduce flow?
assessment_items.answer: It can increase queues, handoffs and multitasking, lengthening end-to-end delivery time.

assessment_items.question: Is Scrum required to be Agile?
assessment_items.answer: No. Scrum is one framework; agile principles can be expressed through other iterative, flow-based or hybrid approaches.

title: Senior Agile Interview: Adaptation, Flow and Enterprise Value
summary: Senior scenarios testing agile judgment across teams, products, metrics and organizational constraints.

questions.question: A team hits every iteration commitment but customers are unhappy. What do you challenge?
When would you choose flow over fixed iterations?
answer_points: need to manage WIP and lead time
